rows.selection_reason: No completed experiments exist, so the key uncertainty is whether basic RNA features alone provide useful signal before adding image, multiprofile aggregation, or fusion. config_001 tests this minimal RNA-only, single-profile PCA baseline and establishes a performance floor for later RNA encoder, profile, and multimodal comparisons. It is the best first budget use because it is simple, avoids confounding multiple design choices, and gives a reference point for deciding whether added complexity is warranted.

The only completed experiment is an RNA-only single-profile PCA baseline with validation accuracy 0.4849 and F1 0.4639, leaving major uncertainty about whether image features are competitive or useful. config_010 tests an image-only single-profile ResNet-50 baseline, changing modality while keeping the profile setting simple and using a standard image encoder. This is the best next experiment because it establishes a key modality baseline needed to interpret future multimodal results and to determine whether image information should be pursued, fused, or deprioritized under a limited budget.

RNA-only PCA single-profile is much stronger than image-only ResNet single-profile, so the RNA branch is the most promising direction. The key uncertainty is whether multiprofile aggregation adds value without changing the RNA representation. config_002 keeps the same pca_n2000 encoder and adds only multiprofile with simple avgpool, isolating the profile/aggregation effect while exploiting the current best baseline. This is a low-risk, informative next step before investing in transformer aggregation, new RNA encoders, or multimodal fusion.

The strongest evidence is that multiprofile RNA with PCA and avgpool (config_002, 0.591 accuracy / 0.573 F1) clearly outperforms single-profile RNA (config_001) and that image-only ResNet is weak. The main remaining uncertainty in this promising RNA direction is whether transformer aggregation improves over avgpool for multiple profiles. config_003 changes only aggregation, so it cleanly tests aggregation complexity while preserving the best current profile and encoder; it either yields a stronger RNA baseline or confirms avgpool, making it an efficient next step before testing new encoders or multimodal fusion.

The strongest completed result is RNA multiprofile with avgpool and PCA (config_002: accuracy 0.591, F1 0.573), clearly better than single-profile PCA and multiprofile transformer aggregation, while image-only ResNet50 is weak. The main remaining uncertainty for the current best direction is whether a stronger RNA representation can improve performance without changing profile or aggregation. config_008 tests scGPT under the same multiprofile/avgpool setting, isolating the effect of RNA representation and extending the most promising evidence before moving to multimodal fusion.

Existing evidence shows RNA multiprofile with PCA and avgpool is the strongest setting (0.591 accuracy, 0.573 F1), outperforming single-profile RNA, transformer aggregation, and scGPT avgpool; image-only ResNet50 is weak (0.208), leaving uncertainty whether image features can add complementary signal. config_018 keeps the best RNA profile/aggregation and adds the already-tested ResNet50 image encoder with a simple concat fusion, directly testing whether multimodal fusion improves over the best RNA-only baseline. It is the best next budget use because it exploits the strongest RNA evidence while probing the central multimodal/fusion question with minimal additional confounds, using a simple fusion baseline before trying weighted fusion or stronger image encoders.

The current best is config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, PCA, ResNet50, avgpool, concat) with 0.619 accuracy / 0.610 F1, only modestly above the strong RNA-only multiprofile avgpool baseline, while image-only ResNet50 is weak. This leaves uncertainty about whether the image branch is limited by its encoder. config_024 changes only the image encoder to ImageNet ViT-L while keeping profile, aggregation, and concat fusion fixed, directly testing image representation. It is the best next budget use because it is a clean exploitation of the best setting and can clarify whether a stronger visual encoder can materially improve multimodal performance before further fusion or RNA-encoder changes.

Current evidence identifies multimodal multiprofile PCA with avgpool and concat as the strongest direction: config_018 has 0.619 accuracy and 0.610 F1, while config_024 has slightly higher accuracy but lower F1. The accuracy difference is small, and F1 slightly favors the resnet50 setting. Fusion strategy is still untested in this promising multimodal region. config_019 changes only fusion from concat to weighted relative to config_018, isolating whether weighted fusion can improve the already strong RNA+image pipeline. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the best-supported direction, tests an important unexplored design choice, and may either find a new best configuration or confirm that concat is sufficient.

The strongest evidence is for multimodal, multiprofile, PCA-RNA, avgpool models: weighted fusion with ResNet50 is best so far (0.639 acc / 0.620 F1), while ViT-L with concat is close (0.629 acc / 0.599 F1). This leaves an important missing comparison: whether ViT-L also benefits from weighted fusion. config_025 tests that by changing only fusion from concat to weighted relative to config_024, or only image encoder from ResNet50 to ViT-L relative to config_019. It is the best next experiment because it exploits the current best design direction while isolating the image-encoder/fusion interaction under the strongest known profile and aggregation settings.

The strongest evidence is config_019: multimodal, multiprofile, PCA, ResNet50, avgpool, weighted fusion, with the best validation accuracy and F1. Weighted fusion also consistently outperformed concat, and multiprofile avgpool helped in RNA-only models. The main uncertainty is whether multiprofile aggregation is actually needed in the multimodal setting, since singleprofile multimodal with the same weighted PCA-ResNet design is untested. config_017 tests this by switching to singleprofile while keeping the best-supported fusion, image encoder, and RNA encoder. It is a high-value next step because it exploits the current best direction, may produce a competitive simpler model, and clarifies whether multiprofile complexity is worth retaining under a limited budget.
